data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary distribution of Unreal Engine using a manual download protocol with pinned checksums. The .install script creates a directory with 777 permissions, which is poor security hygiene but not a malicious injection. The only disagreement stems from a transient API error in the Qwen model when reviewing a standard MIME XML file, which Deepseek correctly assessed as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: Qwen returned 'inconclusive' solely due to an HTTP 400 API error when attempting to audit 'unreal-engine.xml'. Deepseek successfully audited the same file and correctly identified it as a benign MIME type definition. There is no substantive disagreement on security risks.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to review 'unreal-engine.xml' due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Transient API errors on individual non-executable files (like XML or desktop entries) should not force an overall 'inconclusive' package verdict if the file is easily identifiable as benign metadata.

Models are correctly distinguishing between poor packaging hygiene (e.g., 777 permissions in .install) and actual malicious supply-chain injections, avoiding false positives on upstream behavior or style choices.
